headline: A long stretch of dry, mild weather is in store for New York, with highs in the 60s Wednesday through Sunday and no significant weather expected.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Tuesday is dry with high pressure overhead and highs slightly above normal. Winds are light from the northwest early, around 10 knots (about 10 mph) by late morning and afternoon, shifting to come from the west. Tuesday night stays dry and clear with light winds.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Wednesday through Friday stay dry as a large area of high pressure builds over the middle of the country and expands east. Highs reach 60–65 degrees across the region, well above normal. Nights warm up more slowly because the dry air and clear skies let temperatures drop after sunset.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Dry, mild weather continues through at least Saturday and possibly the whole weekend, with highs still 60–65 through Sunday. A cold front passing Sunday night into Monday may bring a few showers, but no significant impacts are expected.

coast: High pressure keeps the waters calm all week, with no advisories: winds mostly from the northwest to west under 15 knots and ocean seas no higher than 2–3 ft.
watch_for: A few showers possible with a cold front Sunday night into Monday.
confidence: High confidence in dry, mild weather through Saturday; slightly less certainty about whether Sunday stays dry ahead of the cold front.
